trust_decision.summary: A client-supplied record message 'path' is written straight into object data without rejecting __proto__/constructor/prototype segments: the generic tokenizer splits the path and assigns/reads member by member, so one record PATCH can reach Object.prototype; the decision point is tokenize/setValue in src/utils/json-path.ts, reached from the record transition and, before it, from the valve permission check that merges the patch into a cache-loaded copy.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is only 'prototype pollution'; the one generic path-assignment primitive (setValue) is what a search for a path write lands on, and every record patch goes through it.

fix_sites.entry_point: Record write message carrying a path (PATCH / CREATEANDPATCH / ERASE, and CREATEANDUPDATE with a path) from the ws-text, ws-json and HTTP-JIF endpoints
The same record patch message, evaluated by the valve permission handler before the record handler runs, when a rule references data/oldData
fix_sites.module_kind: permission service (rule-data merge on a cache-loaded copy)

fix_sites.entry_point: Every caller of setValue/getValue: the record transition, the permission valve, and the server-side deepstream.set() config API (src/deepstream.io.ts:121-122)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It only merges the patch into a throwaway deep copy used to evaluate a permission rule, the actual record write is validated later in the transition, and the valve rule only reads data when the operator writes a data-referencing rule (the shipped conf/permissions.yml has none) - so polluting that copy looks harmless.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valve rules that read data.* on a PATCH must still see the patch merged onto the loaded record (e.g. write: 'data.lastname === "Hempel"'); a fix that stops the valve merging patch data, or refuses every patch that reaches the valve, breaks legitimate write rules.

O6_input_shapes: a.__proto__.polluted (forbidden key as a nested segment)
__proto__ alone (single segment swaps the record object's prototype)
legitimate paths that must keep working: items[0].name, address.99.street.1, animals[ 1 ], animals.name.length, user_proto.foo

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Server-side config API: deepstream.set(key, value) resolves the key with getValue(config, key) and then calls setValue(config, key, value), so key '__proto__' resolves to Object.prototype (not undefined) and is assigned as the config object's prototype
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a server-side option API whose key and value come from the embedding application, not from a connected client, and it targets the config object's own prototype rather than Object.prototype
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src root module, outside src/handlers/record and src/services/permission/valve; 1 file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A record-patch route on the MQTT endpoint that builds a path from the topic/payload and feeds RecordTransition
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The MQTT endpoint already carries record updates and explicitly answers patches with 'Patches are not currently supported via the MQTT API' (src/connection-endpoint/mqtt/socket-wrapper-factory.ts:168-171); supporting them is the obvious next step and would reuse the same setValue sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Reusing the project's own recursive merge() for record data (upserts/defaults) instead of json-path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: merge() iterates 'for (key in objB)' and does objA[key] = objA[key] || {}, the same prototype-key hazard; a maintainer adding a merge/defaults route for records would naturally reach for the existing helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An optional path on list.write, mapped to CREATEANDPATCH exactly as record.write already is
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: record.write is mapped to CREATEANDPATCH whenever msg.path is set (src/jif/jif-handler.ts:65-81); a maintainer extending the HTTP/JIF list API would copy that shape.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via path-based record writes

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=22, npm, tsc via scripts/tsc.sh, ts-node/register/transpile-only, mocha + chai
O10_build.project_tests: npm test runs mocha 'src/**/*.spec.ts'; relevant: src/utils/json-path.spec.ts, src/handlers/record/record-transition.spec.ts, src/handlers/record/record-handler.spec.ts, src/services/permission/valve/config-permission-record-patch.spec.ts, src/services/permission/valve/config-permission-basic.spec.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard record-transition.add() alone with a shape-fitted string test (e.g. path.includes('__proto__')), which leaves the constructor.prototype shape and the valve's cache-copy merge route open.

out_of_scope_notes: src/utils/utils.ts:77-100 merge() recursively assigns for-in keys and would pollute through a '__proto__' key, but it is only fed by server config files and CLI args (src/deepstream.io.ts:469, src/config/js-yaml-loader.ts:163), not by a connected client; not pursued.
